name: Pets.com
tierWhy: Pets.com, Inc. was dissolved and liquidated in 2001–2004; pets.com only redirects to PetSmart and nothing trades under the name.[^6][^10][^36]

dates.text: went public on the Nasdaq at $11 a share
announced it was winding down and laid off about 255 of 320 employees
ran its sock puppet commercial during Super Bowl XXXIV

title: Pets.com (1998–2000): sock puppet, shipping losses
description: Pets.com sold pet supplies online and ran a Super Bowl ad. It never sold a quarter’s goods for more than they cost to buy and ship, and wound down in 2000.

card.blurb: The most famous mascot of the dot-com era, Amazon as its biggest shareholder, and a Super Bowl ad. It never sold a quarter’s goods for more than they cost to deliver.

hero.dates: Began operating Feb 17, 1999. Announced its wind-down Nov 7, 2000.
hero.standfirst: The company’s slogan was “Because pets can’t drive.” Its business model didn’t get far either.
hero.deck: Pets.com was an online pet store with the most famous mascot of the [dot-com era](/category/dotcom/), Amazon as its biggest shareholder and a Super Bowl ad, and it announced its wind-down in November 2000. In 270 days as a public company it never sold a single quarter’s goods for more than they cost to buy and ship.
hero.artCaption: Original illustration in the spirit of the mascot, with the company’s slogan. Not the trademarked character.

findings.title: It lost money before marketing.
findings.text: Cost of goods sold, including shipping, was higher than sales in every quarter it reported. Its prospectus put shipping costs at 100–110% of revenue.[^1]

findings.title: It bought fame, not loyalty.
findings.text: It spent $103.1M on marketing & sales over six quarters against $31.6M in sales.[^4]

findings.title: It went public weeks before the crash.
findings.text: The IPO priced on Feb 11, 2000. The Nasdaq peaked on Mar 10.[^26]

findings.title: No one would refinance it.
findings.text: Fewer than 8 of the 50+ buyers and investors Merrill Lynch approached would even visit.[^5]

findings.title: The idea wasn’t wrong.
findings.text: Chewy did $11.86B in sales in FY2024, built on subscriptions and positive gross margins.[^19]
